content.title: Luka Dončić injures hamstring in Lakers’ blowout loss to Thunder
content.text: OKLAHOMA CITY — What was supposed to be an MVP-candidate showdown ended as badly as possible for the Los Angeles Lakers, with LA getting blown out 139-96 and — much more importantly — Luka Dončić limping off the court midway through the third quarter with a left hamstring injury.A Friday MRI revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain that will sideline Dončić for at least the rest of the regular season, the team announced.With the Lakers trailing 90-58 and 7:39 remaining, Dončić came up limping after driving to the basket against Jalen Williams. Dončić took the weight off his left leg before lying down on the baseline. The Lakers called a timeout, and Dončić limped to the back. He reacted as if something significant had occurred, flipping the ball behind his back and out of bounds, surrendering the possession.“At this juncture of the season, it’s the last thing you want to see,” LeBron James said after the game. “Especially, anybody on our team, but when you have an MVP candidate on your team, the last thing you want to see is somebody go down with a hamstring injury.”Your browser does not support the video tag.The Lakers trailed by at least 30 points most of the game after a disastrous start in which they repeatedly turned the ball over against the Thunder’s pressure. Dončić, who was named the Western Conference Player of the Month for March earlier in the day, was having his worst game in weeks. He made just 3-of-10 from the field with six turnovers before exiting after 25 minutes. He began grabbing at his hamstring after a jumping pass to Luke Kennard late in the first half. “We checked him out, he got worked on, he was cleared,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said of that incident. “Again, we’re not going to put a player at risk.Dončić’s second-half exit came after teammate Austin Reaves needed a trip to the locker room in the first quarter. With the Lakers already being badly beaten, Reaves began grabbing at his left side after he tipped a loose ball to himself for a rebound. He stayed in the game for multiple minutes, clearly reaching at his left side.Reaves, who has been dealing with multiple nagging minor injuries, returned to the court midway through the second period. He left for good in the third quarter as the NBA’s defending champions were routing the Lakers.Thursday was Dončić’s 64th game this season. The NBA requires players to play in at least 65 games to be considered for several postseason awards, so Dončić must participate in one of the Lakers’ final five games to be eligible for MVP and all-NBA. (Dončić was suspended for the Lakers’ win Monday against Washington after receiving his 16th technical foul in the previous game.)Your browser does not support the video tag.Dončić missed four games with a left hamstring injury before the All-Star break. He’d played in 21 of the Lakers’ next 22 games (only missing for the suspension) while averaging 35.8 points on 25 shot attempts and 7.8 assists per game. His 38.1 usage rate leads the NBA and is a career high.The Lakers’ next game is Sunday in Dallas against Dončić’s former team, the Mavericks. Apr 16, 2026Connections: Sports EditionSpot the pattern.
